Sebastian's cards and handout, take two

Rebuilt from research (what makes a card feel good), with much less on them. One look on both sides, no white/black split, the website's own colors. The QR you liked is the hero on the back. Each direction is shown as it would look printed: the colors are soft-proofed for print, so the blue looks deeper and calmer here than on the website (that's how ink on paper comes out). Before ordering, we check FedEx's print preview and print a single handout first; if the colour looks off, we stop.

A Sello

A seal: a bold blue circle stamp with the S runs off the edge; his name sits quietly beside it. The back carries a small piece of the same circle.

B Frase

The line leads: "Para que no se le pase nada." Big and warm on the card and the handout; the brand sits small.

C Relieve

Tone-on-tone: a big S in a deeper vanilla runs off two edges like an emboss; quiet, warm, nothing that can print as a stain.

What stays the same in all three

  • Card: SANO Systems, Sebastian, his role, his cell, and the QR (opens the website's home page in Spanish, tagged to him). Frase adds its one line; that's it.
  • Handout: one feeling, one supporting line, the QR, his name. The website carries everything else. No prices.
  • The S is a clean one-color version of the same logo shape (the glass-texture version turns muddy at card size).
  • Printing at FedEx Office, same day: cards on 100 lb matte cover, $18.75 for 100. Handouts as 5.5 × 8.5 postcards: FedEx lists $36.99 per 50 double-sided, so 100 + 100 comes to about $100.38 with tax, a dollar over your $100. Your call: allow the extra dollar, or print the handouts single-sided in Spanish (about $87). We'll confirm the exact price, and whether the handout can print edge to edge, in FedEx's cart before ordering.
  • The phone number shown is a made-up sample (PRUEBA). His real cell goes in only after he OKs printing it on Monday's paperwork. Sebastian reads every Spanish line and confirms how he spells his name (Sebastian / Sebastián) on Monday.

One question with your pick

Your ruling was Spanish front, English back. With so little text now, these card backs are Spanish-first with one English line under it (the QR goes to the Spanish site either way). Keep it that way, or make the back fully English?

Your pick: tell Claude "cards A", "cards B" or "cards C" (and "back as is" or "back in English"), or what to change.
